column1: # NAME-keyed resolutions for '!Global type conflicts found by scripts/assemble.py.
# globals_final.tsv and globals_corrections.tsv are keyed by ADDRESS. A conflict surfaced
# by the assembler is keyed by NAME, because a '!Global pragma carries no address -- so
# neither of those files can express "the Global spelled g_object108 is TGadget, not
# Object". This file closes that gap. It is consulted only for a name where two bodies
# declared different types; a name with one agreed type never reaches it.
# BEFORE ADDING A ROW, check which defect you actually have. They look identical in the
#   TYPE CONFLICT    one module slot, two bodies disagreeing about its type -> a row here.
#   NAME COLLISION   two DIFFERENT module slots that were given the same name by different
#                    workers. Both types are right. Forcing one type here is WRONG; rename
#                    one Global in its file instead (g_wheel -> g_roulettewheel and
#                    g_ball -> g_roul_ball are the worked precedents).
# The assembler cannot tell them apart, because the address lives in a prose comment and
# not in the pragma. Read the addresses in the files before deciding.
# The declared type picks the vtable slot for every call through the Global, so a row here
# is a codegen claim, not a formatting preference. Cite the evidence.

column3: evidence

0x00c61cf8, declared by four bodies: TGadget.GetActiveGadgetName and TScreen.TextEntered say TGadget, TInputBox.GetInputText and TScreen_Pairs.ClickCard say Object. TGadget satisfies all four sites and Object satisfies only two, so TGadget is the only consistent reading. GetActiveGadgetName's verified body is `If g_Object108 <> Null Then Return g_Object108.name` -- `name` is TGadget field 2 (object_model.json), and Object has no such member, so bcc rejects the Object spelling outright ("Identifier 'name' not found"). The two Object sites immediately downcast (`TInputBox(g_Object108)`, `TButton(g_Object108)`) and both TInputBox and TButton Extend TGadget per class_tables.tsv, so those casts are equally legal from TGadget. Nothing anywhere requires the weaker type.

column1: # --- wave 9 (worker `w9_conflicts`): the four conflicts named in docs/specs/23-assembly.md
# Two were TYPE CONFLICTS; two were NAME COLLISIONS and were fixed by renaming, per the
# rule above. Full evidence in globals_corrections.tsv (VA-keyed) and
# docs/reconstruction/wave9-conflicts.md. All 16 touched files re-verified MATCH.
# NOTE g_object108 above is a FIFTH name for 0x00C61CF8 -- the same slot as g_activegadget
# below, reached independently and with the same answer (TGadget). The corpus spelled that
# one module Global g_activegadget, g_selectedgadget, g_object108, and (in prose)
# g_curgadget. Two workers resolving it separately is itself the finding: the conflict
# report is keyed by name, so ONE defective slot can surface as several unrelated-looking
# rows. Merging the names is the real fix; the type row only stops the bleeding.

column3: 0x00C61CF8. Object in 7 files vs TGadget in 8. TGadget: +0x40 is loaded, compared against 0x005B95D0 (the empty function bcc stores into an uncalled ()i field) and then CALLED at 0x00511516 -- a function-pointer field, and only TGadget.fHit()i fits among the 6 Types carrying the whole observed slot+field set. 0x00514C5D returns +0x0C directly as $ with the empty-string literal as the null fallback = name$. Slot 0x6C is called with two String args (0x00C5D680="FFFFFF") = SetColour($,$)i; slot 0x70 = SetAlph(f). The stored value is a bbObjectDowncast to 0x00C62150 = TGadget (0x005123AB), so the declared type must be TGadget or an ancestor -- which eliminates the other 5 candidates, all of which Extend Object directly and are unrelated to TGadget. 14 release sites, so a reference, not an Int.

NAME COLLISION IN REVERSE -- not a distinct Global at all. TScreen.MouseSelection stored "g_selectedgadget" at 0x005123F5/0x0051242D and TScreen_Options.ButtonCam read "g_selectedgadget" at 0x005211C6; both addresses are 0x00C61CF8, i.e. g_activegadget. There is no selected-gadget slot. Both files renamed to g_activegadget:TGadget; this row exists only so the name cannot come back.

0x00C6F028, was g_contractoffer_tplayer (TPlayer in 1 file, TProfile in 3) and g_np_profile (TProfile) and g_profile (TProfile in 6). Construction site 0x004BB9E2: `push 0x00C6A4C0; call bbObjectNew`, and 0x00C6A4C0 is TProfile's class table => New TProfile. Independently the 39 slots dispatched directly through it intersect to exactly 1 of 348 scopes. TPlayer is impossible on size alone: instance_size 396 (0x18C) cannot hold the +0x1A4 field that TContractOffer.EraseInterestedClubs writes through this Global; TProfile is 544 (0x220). The TPlayer row came from "only TPlayer has slots 0x30/0x34/0x3C/0x40" -- unsound, 143 Types share them. The NAME encoded the wrong guess, so it was retired in favour of the corpus-majority g_profile.

NAME COLLISION. 0x00C6BBBC, formerly `g_wheel`, which the corpus also used for the unrelated 0x00C6BCB4. Assigned at 0x00575533 from call [0x00C6BE3C] = TRouletteWheel classtable (0x00C6BE0C) + 0x30 = Create():TRouletteWheel -- a factory's declared return type. Renamed in TRoulette.Draw.bmx; pairs with 0x00C6BBC0 g_roul_ball:TRouletteBall, built by the same initialiser at 0x00575511.

NAME COLLISION, the surviving half. 0x00C6BCB4, assigned at 0x00575B06 from LoadImageChecked (0x004BC372, sig ($,i):TImage) loading GameMedia/Images/Casino/Roulette/Wheel.png, then passed to MidHandleImage. No slot is ever dispatched through it and no field is read off it, so the type rests entirely on the factory return type. Pairs with 0x00C6BCB8 g_wheelinner:TImage. BOTH original types were right; only the shared name was wrong, which is why no type row could have fixed this one.

0x00C6C81C, TGadget[] in TScreen_Pairs.ResetButtonPositions vs TButton[] in TScreen_Pairs.UpdateFaces. Genuine TYPE CONFLICT, not a name collision: UpdateFaces loads the same absolute 0x00C6C81C at 0x005793C2 and 0x005793DC. TButton is forced by UpdateFaces alone -- both element dispatches are `call dword ptr [eax+0x90]` = slot 144, and slot 144 is TButton.SetIcon(:TImage)i in object_model.json. TGadget's table ENDS at slot 132 (SetPosition), so 0x90 is not a TGadget slot at all and the TGadget spelling cannot compile that call. ResetButtonPositions is simply under-determined and says so in its own header: it uses only slot 132 (SetPosition, inherited) and field +0x38 (TGadget.alive), both of which TButton inherits unchanged, so it emits identical bytes either way. class_tables.tsv: TButton super = TGadget, and TButton's fields start at 92 immediately after TGadget's last at 88, so the inheritance is direct and no slot shifts. SIZE ADDED 2026-08-15: this row resolved the TYPE conflict but left the array unsized (length 0), so every index threw in a -d build -- g_pairs_buttons[0..15] in TScreen_Pairs.CreateScreen was the case that surfaced it. Size 16 read from module_globals_decoded.tsv at the VA above. Because the name was already present here, both automated size passes skipped it.

column3: 0x00C61700. 4 files agree TScreen (TProfile.UpdateRelationship, TScreen.GetInput, TScreen.Render, TScreen.TextEntered) vs 1 file (TTable.UpdateActivated) declaring Object. TTable.UpdateActivated's own header says the weaker spelling was a choice, not a finding: "only compared against bbNullObject here, so the declared type does not reach codegen; left as Object" -- i.e. that file is silent on the true type and TScreen satisfies it trivially (any type compares against Null). TScreen.Render's own construction/dispatch site is unambiguous: `g_Object101.Draw()` resolves to TScreen's own Draw() slot, which Object does not have at all -- Object cannot compile that call, so TScreen is the only spelling consistent with every site.

0x00C5D1B4. SIZE, not type. The ten control-binding arrays are declared `Int[]` (length 0) by TOptions.LoadOptions' '!Global pragmas, so every `g_opt_ctrlX[0] = ...` threw "Attempt to index array element beyond array length" -- invisible in a release build, which silently swallows array overruns (blitzmax-language-guide 18.26), and fatal in -d. The real size is 2 and it is proven by VA, not inferred: module_globals_decoded.tsv read `_bbArrayNew1D(Int, 2)` at this exact address (as g_options_arr02, the auto-generated VA-keyed name for the same slot). LoadOptions' own header states the layout -- "Index 0 = keyboard (+0x18), index 1 = joystick (+0x1C)" -- which is why the file reads both a k_* and a j_* value for each binding. assemble.py's array_sizes pass could not fix this itself because it matches on NAME and the two tables spell this slot differently.
